items.note: Errors match the system: invalid fields get a 2px danger border, the focused one adds a pink halo and ink ring, and each message is ink text after a small red glyph, all inside a white ink-hairline panel under the lemon header band. It keeps the ink-hairline character of the reference's dense form screen, and a person can see which fields to fix and how. The black footer that rc.3 was missing is now there.

The dark mode is a faithful inversion. Boxes are one step lighter than the black ground with light hairlines, the lemon band is unchanged, and the current nav pill turns white, as in the reference's dark capture. The danger borders and the pink focus halo on the empty field stay clear against the dark inputs.

The error treatment holds up on the phone: thick red borders, a halo-plus-ink ring on the focused field, and full-width stacked actions in a ruled panel. The section links above the lemon band wrap into two loose rows with one link alone on the second line. The reference keeps its pill row compact on one line.

The page itself is on-system: the pink save button sits lifted on its hard shadow next to an outline reset. But the saved outcome is only an 8px teal dot and the word 'Saved', loose beside the buttons, with no frame or panel. That is even quieter than rc.3's outline pill, and far weaker than the error state on the same form.

Dark mode has the same bare 'Saved' dot-and-word. The tiny teal dot almost disappears on the dark panel, so the success is hard to notice. The reference treats outcomes as framed, picked-up ink panels.

On the phone the confirmation is a dot and a word under the full-width save and reset buttons, inside the form panel. It reads as an afterthought rather than a designed toast or status pill in the system's language.

The dialog is a white ink panel with the static hard black shadow over a flat overlay. It has a ruled header holding a title-size question and a bordered close button, a ruled footer with an outline cancel and a pink confirm, and the plan cards behind show notched price flags and a pink selected border. The consequence and the next step read clearly, in the reference's flat, drawn idiom.

In dark mode the dialog is a raised dark panel with light hairline rules and a 35%-white hard shadow, so it still reads as picked up off the page. The pink confirm stays the one hot action, and the flags and selected border are unchanged from light, as rule 10 asks.

On the phone the dialog becomes a full-width bottom sheet: an ink-ruled header with a close box, the body text, and stacked pink confirm over outline cancel. It is clear and on-system. The overlay covering only the first viewport comes from the full-page capture, not from the design.

The mismatch field has the thick danger border plus focus ring and a plain ink message after a red glyph. The strength hint uses a status dot, and the teal header band and ruled sessions table follow the reference's form language. The fields are only about 400px wide in a panel over 1000px wide, so more than half the panel is empty. The reference's form panel fills its width.

Dark mode inverts the panel correctly and keeps the teal band intact. The error ring and message stay legible. The same half-empty panel remains, with narrow fields floating at the left of a wide box.

On the phone the fields fill the panel. The error border and message are clear, and the full-width pink update button is the obvious next step, under a compact teal band. It is close to the reference's phone app screen in rhythm and hairline character.

The keyboard focus on a sidebar link is drawn as a thick ink outline pill next to the filled black current pill, which is clearly the system's own ring. Below it, the periwinkle band with a notched count flag and the ruled switch rows in white boxes sit close to the reference's settings screen.

In dark mode the focus ring turns to a light outline pill beside the white current pill, so focus stays easy to see. The periwinkle band and pink flag are unchanged, and the switch rows are ruled with light hairlines on raised boxes.

The focus ring on the phone's section links is clear and drawn in ink, but the link row wraps and leaves one link alone on a second line. Below that, the periwinkle band, flag and ruled switch panel follow the reference's phone app screen well.

findings.summary: The saved confirmation is still the quietest state on the form. It is now only an 8px teal dot and the word 'Saved' sitting loose next to the buttons, with no pill or panel, and in dark the dot nearly disappears. The reference draws outcomes as framed, picked-up ink pieces (a white ink panel with a static hard shadow, or a status pill), and the errors on this same form are far more designed. rc.3 named this gap and it has not closed; it has regressed slightly.

On the password form, the fields are fixed at about 400px inside a panel over 1000px wide, so more than half of the white panel is empty space to the right. The reference's form panel is filled by its fields and preview, with no dead half. rc.3 named this and it is unchanged.

On phones, the section links above the header band wrap into two loose rows, with the last link alone on the second line, which adds a tall, untidy strip above the band. The reference keeps its phone pill row compact on one line.
